title: Oman and Iran Hold UNGA Talks on Hormuz Navigation, With Oman as Potential Mediator
detail: Oman and Iran held bilateral talks on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York on September 26, focusing on Hormuz navigation and regional tensions. Oman, which has historically served as a back-channel between Iran and Western powers, is exploring a potential mediation role as diplomatic efforts to reopen the strait continue. The talks add another regional diplomatic track alongside the Qatari and Pakistani channels Iran has been using to relay conditions to Washington.

media.caption: Oman and Iran hold talks on Hormuz navigation at the UN General Assembly

title: Trump Privately Rejects Iran's Seven-Day Hormuz Reopening Plan, Expects Bombing to Resume After Midterms — WSJ
detail: The Wall Street Journal reported Sep 26 that President Trump has rejected Iran's seven-day roadmap to reopen the Strait of Hormuz -- the plan Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi presented at the UN General Assembly on Sep 25 -- and told aides he considers a renewed US bombing campaign against Iran likely after the November midterm elections. Officials described Trump as privately skeptical Iran will meet his demands, though he remains reluctant to resume major combat operations for now and the scope of any envisioned strikes is unclear; his views could still shift depending on the midterm outcome. There was no official Washington statement on the proposal itself, and Reuters separately described the sidelines contacts in New York as 'positive and constructive.' The report landed as Brent crude closed Friday Sep 25 at $104.32/bbl, down 2.1% ($2.28) from Thursday's $106.60 settle, as markets had priced in some chance of Iran's proposal advancing before news of the rejection broke.

media.caption: Trump reportedly rejected Iran's seven-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, per WSJ
